newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Denmark to switch South African aid to region.
newsitem.headline: Denmark to switch South African aid to region.

text.p: Denmark, pronouncing its five-year aid relationship with South Africa a success, will shift its focus to the southern African region from 1998, Development Cooperation Minister Poul Nielson said on Tuesday.
Nielson, in South Africa to review the success of a 750 million crown transitional aid package, said the programme launched in 1994 would be wound down on schedule after 1998.
"South Africa has been a success," he said.
"I would say South Africa is an example where the quality and intensity and creativity of the relationship has been more important to both sides than resources in the form of money."
Nielson said a programme twinning Danish companies with emerging black businesses in South Africa would be the last aid project to go around 2001 or 2002.
Denmark would continue to inject around a billion crowns a year into southern Africa, but South Africa's share would be switched to other countries in the region after 1998.
He hoped South Africa would participate in the regional aid programme and share its experience with other countries in the Southern African Development Community (SADC).
"We hope to stimulate regional cooperation within the SADC and that South Africa will not be a recipient, but a partner in the region," he said.
Nielson said Denmark would continue to work with South Africa on environmental programmes, but would not provide the sort of direct aid it committed after white rule ended in 1994.
Denmark was one of the major supporters of President Nelson Mandela's African National Congress during its struggle against white rule.
